task_title: Load-hygiene: bridge integration tests run in-process, real-exec parity seam kept
task_criteria: Bridge verdict assertions run in-process: plugin/test_interruptor_integration.py drives interruptor_bridge.main() via _bridge_main_inproc for every bridge-verdict assertion; the file contains exactly 2 real subprocess.run call sites - the _run_cli helper used by CLI-level tests (there the process boundary IS the subject, by design) and the single real spawn inside test_bridge_real_exec_parity, which runs the real python3 interruptor_bridge.py and asserts byte-identical stdout and equal rc against the in-process path across the BRIDGE_PARITY_INPUTS set (allow, block, modify, empty-schema, null). A third grep hit for the literal string subprocess.run is a docstring mention, not a call site.

Structural seam test test_bridge_in_process_path_never_spawns_a_process patches subprocess.run to raise and the in-process path still answers allow; it warms the engine import explicitly so isolated and -k runs behave like full-file runs
Measured: file wall time 7.8s before vs 4.1s after; full suite on merged main reports 1018 passed, 7 skipped; zero tests deleted, zero skip marks added (35 to 37 tests in the file, +2 seam tests)
ruff check clean on the changed file (uvx ruff check plugin/test_interruptor_integration.py) and full suite green on merged main at HEAD ec3e645 or later
CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] carries the VERSION-002 entry with the before/after numbers
